title: How do we subtract a fraction from another, as indicated?
description: Three subtractions are worded with the word from. The fraction after from is the one we start with. Each pair is changed to the same bottom number, and then the tops are taken away.
teaching_notes: One idea: a fraction from another fraction means the second one is the one we start with. Change both fractions to the same bottom number, take away the tops and keep the bottom. Watch for students who take away in the order the words are written.

source: Subtract as indicated: a) 13/4 from 10/3 b) 18/5 from 23/3 c) 29/7 from 45/7
video_script.why: The child reads the word from correctly, changes each pair to the same bottom number, and takes away the tops the way the book's solved question does.
video_script.substitution: The book's method for taking away fractions with different bottom numbers, used on three subtractions worded with the word from.
video_script.anchor: three subtractions written in a row on the board, as in the book
video_script.payoff_line: The three answers are one twelfth, sixty one fifteenths and sixteen sevenths

final_answer.spoken: one twelfth, sixty one fifteenths and sixteen sevenths

video_script.fraction_reading: thirteen fourths, ten thirds, eighteen fifths, twenty three thirds, twenty nine sevenths, forty five sevenths, forty twelfths, thirty nine twelfths, one twelfth, sixty one fifteenths, sixteen sevenths
never_show: the three answers together in one line before the answer beat
maths_rules: 45/7 − 29/7 = (45 − 29)/7 = 16/7, and 16 and 7 share no factor except 1
video_script.design: One idea: the fraction after the word from is the one we start with, then same bottom number, then take away the tops. The three subtractions stay on the board as the anchor and each step works on one of them in order.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; three lines in a row: 13/4 from 10/3, 18/5 from 23/3, 29/7 from 45/7

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.list: the three lines appear one after another in a row
marks.ask: the word from glows in each line

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book, with three subtractions to do.
<bookmark mark='list'/>Thirteen fourths from ten thirds. Eighteen fifths from twenty three thirds. Twenty nine sevenths from forty five sevenths.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>The word from tells us something about the order. Which fraction do we start with?

beats.on_screen: the three lines hold still and the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a strip cut into 5 equal parts with 4 shaded; 2 shaded parts slide off; the words 2/5 from 4/5 means 4/5 − 2/5

marks.start: the strip with 4 shaded parts glows as the one we start with
marks.take: 2 shaded parts slide off the strip

beats.colours: start fraction = teal, taken away = amber
narration: <bookmark mark='start'/>The word from names the fraction we start with. Two fifths from four fifths means we start with four fifths.
<bookmark mark='take'/>Start with four fifths, and take away two fifths.
<bookmark mark='words'/>The fraction after the word from comes first, and the other fraction is taken away.

marks.given: the three subtractions are written with the fraction after from placed first

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, three subtractions, each starting with the fraction that comes after the word from.

marks.find: the words to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find all three answers.

marks.first: the first subtraction glows with the bottom numbers 3 and 4
marks.ten: 10/3 becomes 40/12 with the multiplier 4 on the top and the bottom
marks.thirteen: 13/4 becomes 39/12 with the multiplier 3 on the top and the bottom

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step one, the first pair has thirds and fourths. Three times four is twelve, so change both to twelfths.
<bookmark mark='same'/>This is the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='ten'/>Multiply ten thirds by four on the top and the bottom. Ten times four is forty. That gives forty twelfths.
<bookmark mark='thirteen'/>Multiply thirteen fourths by three on the top and the bottom. Thirteen times three is thirty nine.
<bookmark mark='take'/>Forty take away thirty nine is one, so we get one twelfth.

marks.second: the second subtraction glows with the bottom numbers 3 and 5
marks.big: the multiplier 5 appears on the top and the bottom of 23/3
marks.small: 18/5 becomes 54/15 with the multiplier 3 on the top and the bottom

narration: <bookmark mark='second'/>Step two, the second pair has thirds and fifths. Three times five is fifteen, so change both to fifteenths.
<bookmark mark='big'/>Multiply the top and the bottom of twenty three thirds by five.
<bookmark mark='times'/>Twenty three times five is one hundred and fifteen. That gives one hundred and fifteen fifteenths.
<bookmark mark='small'/>Multiply the top and the bottom of eighteen fifths by three. Eighteen times three is fifty four.
<bookmark mark='take'/>One hundred and fifteen take away fifty four is sixty one, so we get sixty one fifteenths.
Sixty one and fifteen share no factor except one.

marks.third: the third subtraction glows and the bottom number 7 is shown twice

narration: <bookmark mark='third'/>Step three, the third pair already has the same bottom number, seven.
<bookmark mark='tops'/>Take away the tops and keep the bottom. Forty five take away twenty nine is sixteen.
<bookmark mark='sixteen'/>We get sixteen sevenths. Sixteen and seven share no factor except one.

marks.back: each working answer slides back beside the fraction that was taken away
marks.add: the three sums appear and each one matches its starting fraction

narration: <bookmark mark='back'/>Step four, check by putting each answer back in its question.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Add each answer to the fraction we took away, and we get back the fraction we started with.

marks.ans: the three answers 1/12, 61/15, 16/7 are boxed in a row

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The three answers are one twelfth, sixty one fifteenths and sixteen sevenths.
